Bangladesh Pesticide Registry Overview

This comprehensive technical field guide provides extension officers, agronomists, pesticide inspectors, and agricultural researchers with an operational, data-driven reference for chemical crop protection across Bangladesh. Derived directly from the DAE/AgriChem master pesticide database, it covers 8,472 registered formulations, 15,983 crop-pest recommendations, and 85 distinct mechanism-of-action groups across IRAC, FRAC, and HRAC classification systems. 7,142 of 8,472 products carry a mapped MoA code (84.3% coverage) — the pipeline maps strictly by active ingredient and leaves ambiguous or unrecorded rows visibly unmapped rather than guessing; each mapped row carries an IRAC / FRAC / HRAC / BIO authority tag.

Regulatory Policy & HHP Risk Matrix

Under PTAC 2026, 1,292 registered formulations (21.05%) meet the criteria for Highly Hazardous Pesticides (HHPs). The four-tier risk classification below is enforced across all extension recommendations and pesticide inspectorate audits. Tier assignment derives from WHO toxicity class, active ingredient hazard profile, and documented field poisoning incidents.

TierCountWHO ClassRepresentative ActivesRegulatory Action
RED607Ia, Ib, IICarbofuran, Monocrotophos, ParaquatPhase-out / Ban in progress
AMBER685II (Moderate)Chlorpyrifos, Cypermethrin, DimethoateRestricted Field Use. Enhanced PPE, MRL surveillance
STANDARD4,123III / UMancozeb, Imidacloprid, Cartap, SulphurStandard GAP. Routine compliance auditing
GREEN23Bio / ExemptBacillus thuringiensis, Trichoderma, AzadirachtinWhitelisted & Subsidized. Expedited registration
⚠ Mandatory Extension Notice: All RED Tier products (607 formulations) are subject to active regulatory review. Extension workers are strictly prohibited from recommending RED Tier active ingredients where viable Standard or Green Tier alternatives exist.

Global Regulatory Discrepancies & Export Compliance

These discrepancies are critical for exporters and processors. Residue violations on shipments to EU, USA, or Japan trigger automatic border rejection and can result in country-wide suspension of import tolerances. The replacements below are selected for efficacy, MRL compliance, and lower mammalian toxicity.

Active MoleculeDAE StatusEU/Global StatusExport ImpactRecommended Replacement
CarbofuranREDBANNED (EU)Severe neurotoxicity; instant rejectionChlorantraniliprole (IRAC 28) or Cartap (IRAC 14)
ChlorpyrifosAMBERBANNED (EU/USA)Developmental neurotoxicity; border recallEmamectin benzoate (IRAC 6), Spinetoram (IRAC 5)
CarbendazimAMBERBANNED (EU)Mutagenic; zero tolerance for Mango/VegetablesAzoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (FRAC 11+3)
ParaquatREDBANNED (>50 countries)Extreme acute toxicity without antidoteGlufosinate ammonium or mechanical tillage

Resistance Management Matrix

IRAC Core Matrix (Insecticides)

Over 75% of insecticide pressure is concentrated in four groups. Repeated application without rotation has produced documented field resistance in BPH, Diamondback Moth, and Brinjal Shoot & Fruit Borer. The rotation partners below are selected to minimize cross-resistance risk and preserve diamide (IRAC 28) efficacy as the last-line chemistry. FRAC & HRAC Matrix (Fungicides & Herbicides)

Fungicide resistance in Bangladesh is dominated by DMI (FRAC 3) and QoI (FRAC 11) chemistry. Single-site mode-of-action fungicides require mandatory co-formulation or alternation with multi-site contact partners (FRAC M01/M03) to delay resistance evolution in rice sheath blight and potato late blight populations. Product counts in the table below are populated live from the dataset.

FRAC 1MBC-Fungicides (Beta-tubulin)189HIGHCarbendazim, Thiophanate-methylLimit to seed treatment; rotate with FRAC 3/M03

Major Crop Protection & Field Rotation

Rice (Boro, Aman & Aus) — 3,884 Recommendations

Rice accounts for the largest share of pesticide recommendations. The rotation schedule below is calibrated for the three Bangladesh rice seasons and accounts for BPH resurgences caused by pyrethroid misapplication. Pymetrozine (IRAC 9B) and flonicamid (IRAC 29) are preferred for BPH management to preserve beneficials and avoid resurgence.

Target Pest/DiseaseFirst Line (MoA)Rotation Partner (MoA)DosagePHI
Brown Planthopper (BPH)Pymetrozine 50% WDG (IRAC 9B)Flonicamid 50% WG (IRAC 29) or Dinotefuran 20% SG (IRAC 4A)300 g/ha14 days
Yellow Stem BorerChlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR (IRAC 28)Cartap 50% SP (IRAC 14) or Fipronil 5% SC10 kg/ha21 days
Sheath BlightHexaconazole 5% EC (FRAC 3)Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (FRAC 11+3)1.0 L/ha15 days
Rice Blast (Leaf/Neck)Tricyclazole 75% WP (FRAC 16.1)Isoprothiolane 40% EC (FRAC 6) or Kasugamycin 3% SL400 g/ha21 days
💡 Avoid Cypermethrin for BPH control — it causes pest resurgence. Spray at plant base.

Tea — 3,338 Recommendations

Tea pest management must respect a 7-day plucking cycle. The recommendations below are sequenced to avoid MRL violations on export shipments. Sulphur is the baseline miticide; propargite and fenazaquin are reserved for sustained outbreaks to preserve predatory mite populations.

Target Pest/DiseasePrimary TreatmentRotation PartnerDosagePHI
Tea Mosquito Bug (Helopeltis)Clothianidin 50% WDG (IRAC 4A)Thiamethoxam 25% WG (IRAC 4A) or Bifenthrin 10% EC60 g/ha7–10 days
Red Spider MiteSulphur 80% WDG (FRAC M02)Propargite 57% EC (IRAC 12C) or Fenazaquin 10% EC2.0 kg/ha14 days
Black Rot / Die BackCopper Oxychloride 50% WP (FRAC M01)Hexaconazole 5% SC (FRAC 3)2.5 kg/ha14 days

Potato, Vegetables & Fruit

Vegetable and fruit production requires careful MoA rotation because of the short cropping cycles and tight PHI windows. Emamectin and chlorantraniliprole are preferred over older OPs and pyrethroids due to lower mammalian toxicity, shorter PHI, and reduced impact on pollinators.

CropMajor PestPrimary MoARotation PartnerDosage

BrinjalShoot & Fruit BorerEmamectin Benzoate 5% SG (IRAC 6)Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (IRAC 28) / Spinosad 45% SC250 g/ha, PHI: 3 days
MangoMango HopperImidacloprid 17.8% SL (IRAC 4A)Lambda-Cyhalothrin 5% EC (IRAC 3A)0.5 ml/L, 2 sprays
TomatoEarly/Late Blight & Fruit BorerAzoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (FRAC 11+3)Mancozeb 80% WP (FRAC M03) + Spinetoram (IRAC 5)1 ml/L, PHI: 7 days

Field Safety, PHI & REI Protocols

Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) & Re-Entry Interval (REI)

The intervals below are minimums derived from worst-case residue decline studies. Always observe the longer of the label PHI or the export-market MRL-based interval. Re-entry intervals assume full PPE compliance during application; unprotected workers must wait 2× the listed REI.

Chemical ClassWHO ClassMin PHIMin REIStewardship Directive
Organophosphates (Chlorpyrifos, Dimethoate)Class II15–21 Days48 HoursHigh dermal absorption. Mandatory chemical-resistant gloves, eye shield, vapor respirator
Carbamates (Carbofuran, Carbosulfan)Class Ib/II21–30 Days48 HoursBroadcast with calibrated applicator only. Never bare hands. Keep livestock off
Synthetic Pyrethroids (Cypermethrin, Lambda)Class II/III7–14 Days24 HoursHighly toxic to aquatic life and honeybees. No application near water bodies or peak flowering
Neonicotinoids (Imidacloprid, Thiamethoxam)Class III7–14 Days12 HoursToxic to pollinators; avoid foliar spray when bees are foraging
Diamides & Avermectins (Chlorantraniliprole, Emamectin)Class III/U3–7 Days12 HoursLow mammalian toxicity. Excellent fit for IPM and short-cycle vegetables
Inorganic Fungicides (Sulphur, Copper Oxy)Class U/III3–5 Days12 HoursEye and skin irritant. Wear goggles and dust mask during WP mixing

Acute Field Poisoning Response

Golden Rule: Immediately remove patient from contaminated zone, strip contaminated clothing, wash skin with clean water and soap. Never induce vomiting if swallowed pesticide contains hydrocarbon solvents (EC formulations) or if patient is unconscious.
Pesticide GroupSymptomsFirst AidMedical Antidote
Organophosphates & CarbamatesPinpoint pupils, salivation, sweating, muscle twitching, nausea, breathing difficultyMaintain airway, recovery position, wash skinAtropine Sulfate (1–2 mg IV/IM). PAM (Pralidoxime) for OPs only
PyrethroidsSkin tingling/burning, dizziness, eye irritation, tremorsWash face/eyes with water. Apply Vitamin E creamSymptomatic; Antihistamines; Diazepam for tremors
Aluminium Phosphide (Gas)Epigastric pain, vomiting, garlic breath, pulmonary edema, shockMove to fresh air. Administer oxygenNo specific antidote. Gastric lavage with KMnO4 (1:10,000); intensive care
Zinc PhosphideNausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, intense thirst, liver/kidney dysfunctionAdminister activated charcoal if consciousGastric lavage with 1% Sodium Bicarbonate; supportive therapy
